explain.say: Have you seen a picture of the Taj Mahal? It was built by one of the Mughal emperors, who ruled much of South Asia for over 300 years. This timeline shows the great emperors, one after another. Let's meet them.

explain.say: Look at the first dot. In 1526 Babur, a prince from Central Asia, won the battle of Panipat, north of Delhi, using cannons and clever tactics. He founded the Mughal empire, and wrote a diary about gardens, fruit and battles. Would you keep a diary like that?

explain.say: Now Akbar, who became emperor at just 13. He built a strong government, invited scholars of many religions to debate, and ended the jizya, a special tax on non-Muslims. Many call him Akbar the Great. Why might fairness make an empire stronger?

explain.say: See the building? Shah Jahan built the Taj Mahal in Agra as a tomb for his wife Mumtaz Mahal, who died in 1631. About 20,000 workers built it over some 20 years. What would you build to remember someone you love?

explain.say: Next, Aurangzeb ruled the largest Mughal empire, but long wars, especially with the Marathas, emptied the treasury. Historians debate how much his strict policies added to unrest. Brilliant work! Wow: the Taj Mahal's marble looks pink at dawn and golden at sunset.

faq.a: Babur, a descendant of Timur and Genghis Khan from Central Asia, founded it after winning the First Battle of Panipat in 1526.

faq.q: Why is Akbar called the Great?
faq.a: Akbar, who ruled from 1556 to 1605, built an efficient government, expanded the empire, and welcomed people of many faiths to his court. He also abolished the jizya tax on non-Muslims.

faq.q: Why was the Taj Mahal built?
faq.a: Shah Jahan built it as a tomb for his wife Mumtaz Mahal, who died in 1631. Built mostly between 1632 and 1653 from white marble, it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

faq.q: Why did the Mughal Empire decline?
faq.a: After Aurangzeb died in 1707, costly wars, weak successors, and rising powers like the Marathas, the Sikhs and later the British East India Company all weakened Mughal rule.
asks: How did the Mughal Empire end?

faq.q: Who was the last Mughal emperor?
faq.a: Bahadur Shah Zafar, also a fine poet. After the uprising of 1857, the British put him on trial and exiled him to Rangoon in Burma, where he died in 1862.
asks: What happened to Bahadur Shah Zafar?

facts: Babur won the First Battle of Panipat in 1526.
The Taj Mahal was built mainly between 1632 and 1653.
Akbar ruled the Mughal Empire from 1556 to 1605.
